content.user_title: Convert Notion Specs Into Implementation Plans
content.value_statement: Teams lose momentum when Notion specs stay disconnected from delivery work. This skill turns specs into linked plans, tasks, and progress updates.
actual_capabilities: Search and fetch Notion specs before planning work.
Extract requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, priorities, gaps, and assumptions.
Choose quick or standard implementation plan templates by project complexity.
Create linked Notion plan pages and task pages through Notion MCP tools.
Update spec, plan, and task status links during progress tracking.
limitations: Requires a connected Notion MCP server and user OAuth access.
Cannot resolve ambiguous product requirements without user clarification.
Depends on the target task database schema and available Notion permissions.
Provides planning workflow guidance, not implementation of application code.

use_cases.title: Turn PRDs into execution plans
use_cases.description: Convert approved Notion product specs into linked implementation plans with requirements, risks, dependencies, and success criteria.

use_cases.title: Break features into scoped tasks
use_cases.description: Create task pages sized for one or two days, with acceptance criteria and links to the source spec and plan.

use_cases.title: Maintain delivery status in Notion
use_cases.description: Keep plans, tasks, blockers, decisions, and milestone summaries synchronized as implementation work progresses.

prompt_templates.title: Create a plan from a spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one approved spec.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find my Notion spec named [spec name], summarize requirements, and create a quick implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Generate tasks for a feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a known task database.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch [spec name], identify the task database, confirm required properties, and create scoped tasks linked to the spec and plan.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a multi-phase rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the standard plan template for [spec name], include phases, dependencies, risks, success criteria, and task links.

prompt_templates.title: Run delivery tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after implementation has started.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the linked spec, plan, and tasks for [project]. Update statuses, blockers, decisions, and the latest progress summary.

output_examples.input: A Notion PRD for a new billing settings page.
output_examples.output: A linked implementation plan with requirements, phases, risks, success criteria, and task pages for design, API, UI, and testing.

output_examples.input: A database migration spec with unclear rollback steps.
output_examples.output: A clarifications block, standard plan recommendation, dependency notes, and scoped tasks after the user answers open questions.

output_examples.input: A project with linked plan and tasks in progress.
output_examples.output: A progress update showing completed work, current blockers, changed decisions, and synchronized task statuses.

best_practices: Confirm the exact Notion spec when search returns multiple results.
Resolve gaps and assumptions before creating tasks or updating project pages.
Keep plan, spec, and task status fields synchronized after each progress update.
anti_patterns: Creating tasks before confirming the task database schema.
Treating unclear acceptance criteria as final requirements.
Updating Notion pages without telling the user what changed.

faq.question: Does this skill require Notion MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It relies on Notion MCP tools to search, fetch, create, and update Notion pages.

faq.question: Can it create implementation tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create scoped task pages when a task database and required properties are available.

faq.question: Can it handle large projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs multi-phase work to a standard implementation plan with phases, risks, dependencies, and success criteria.

faq.question: Will it write application code?
faq.answer: No. It plans implementation work and tracks progress. It does not implement product code by itself.

faq.question: What happens if a spec is ambiguous?
faq.answer: It should capture gaps and assumptions in a clarifications block before creating final plans or tasks.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
